perf.summary: Skip masks whose bit 0 (start vertex) is unset; the start vertex 0 is the only valid DP base, so any subset not containing vertex 0 is dead state.
perf.currentCost: The outer loop iterates all 2^n masks and ProcessCycleMask scans all n last-vertices for each. Roughly half of all masks (those without bit 0) can never be reached from dp[(1<<0)*n+0]=0 yet are fully scanned.
perf.proposedChange: In ProcessCycleMask (or before calling it) skip masks with (mask & 1) == 0: `if ((mask & 1) == 0) continue;`. Equivalently iterate `for (int mask = 1; mask < size; mask += 2)` -- but a simple guard is cleaner and keeps the index meaning.
perf.rationale: Halves the number of (mask,last) inner scans. The Held-Karp DP only ever populates states whose mask includes the fixed start vertex 0, so masks without bit 0 contain only inf entries that fail the `dp[mask*n+last] >= inf` guard anyway -- pure wasted iteration of the inner n-loop and the branch.
perf.risk: Must keep dp init for those masks as inf (it already is via the full init loop) and FindMinBestCycle uses fullMask which has bit 0 set, so unaffected. Semantics preserved exactly: skipped masks produce no transitions today either.

perf.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant base value dp[mask*n+last] and the row base w[last*n] out of the inner u-loop.
perf.currentCost: Each iteration recomputes mask*n+last for the dp read and last*n+u; dp[mask*n+last] is reloaded from memory n times though it is invariant across u.
perf.proposedChange: Add `long baseDp = dp[mask * n + last]; long* wRow = w + last * n; long* dpBase = dp;` before the loop, then use `wRow[u]` and `baseDp + wRow[u]`. Compute `int withU = mask | (1 << u);` once.
perf.rationale: Removes a redundant load and an index multiply from the hot inner loop, shortening the dependency chain. Burst/LLVM may already hoist the invariant load, but strengthening w into a row pointer removes the last*n multiply from every iteration deterministically.
perf.risk: None; dp[mask*n+last] is not written inside this loop (writes target (mask|bit)*n+u with the bit set, so a different slot), so the hoisted value stays valid.
